name: @olai/format
//exports: Two entries, and the second is not product. The `./testlib` subpath is the fixture builder this package's own tests are written against, published so a package ABOVE can write its fixtures the same way — the alternative was @olai/ops growing a byte-identical copy of the same diagnostic, which is exactly the drift src/fixtures.testlib.ts was consolidated to stop.
//dependencies: The bottom of the layering (docs/architecture.md): nothing here can reach a disk, a server or a browser. @olai/git is the one workspace sibling, and it is not a layer violation but the other half of this floor — a LEAF beside this package, on `effect` alone, whose `./state` subpath is pure data (RepoState, Reason) that this package re-exports because it travels the wire. Only that subpath is imported: the main entry shells out to git, and this module is bundled into a browser. fastest-levenshtein is the did-you-mean distance — a focused, dependency-free library rather than eighteen lines of textbook matrix arithmetic we would then own.
//devDependencies: `yaml` is TEST-ONLY and nothing here imports it but src/frontmatter.library.test.ts, which holds this package's frontmatter value subset against the real parser — for every line: we agree, we refuse together, or we are narrower for a reason src/frontmatter.ts's header argues by name. It is deliberately NOT in the module. Putting it there was tried and measured: +10.6 KB brotli on the client's eager bundle (this package is bundled into the browser), for a parse the browser never runs, since a face is built at the decode and its props travel the wire. Same shape as @olai/web's remark-frontmatter, which fences the other half of the same rule — where the block ENDS — and also ships nowhere.
